# Question 2

```{r}
# Step 1 - Prepare metadata for RQ2

# Create a Q2 dataset using the same usable-text posts as RQ1
rq2_data <- alfred_all %>%
  
  # Keep the original row number so each post can be tracked later
  mutate(original_row = row_number()) %>%
  
  # Retain only posts with usable, non-empty text
  filter(text_usable) %>%
  
  # Keep variables required for clustering interpretation
  # and the later link-sharing hypothesis test
  select(
    original_row,
    uri,
    author_handle,
    created_at,
    text,
    has_link
  )

# Check the number of posts and variables retained for RQ2
dim(rq2_data)

# Check the distribution of link-sharing status
table(rq2_data$has_link)
```

```{r}
# Step 2 - Create TF-IDF representation

# Confirm that the cleaned corpus and Q2 metadata contain
# the same number of posts
length(rq1_corpus)
nrow(rq2_data)
```

```{r}
# Create a Term-Document Matrix from the cleaned corpus
rq2_tdm <- TermDocumentMatrix(rq1_corpus)

# Apply TF-IDF weighting
rq2_tfidf <- weightTfIdf(rq2_tdm)

# Check the dimensions of the TF-IDF matrix
dim(rq2_tfidf)
```

```{r}
# Step 3 - Prepare the TF-IDF matrix for clustering

# Convert the TF-IDF matrix so that:
# rows = posts/documents
# columns = terms
rq2_matrix <- t(as.matrix(rq2_tfidf))

# Check the matrix dimensions
dim(rq2_matrix)

# Identify documents with no remaining terms after preprocessing
rq2_row_sums <- rowSums(rq2_matrix)

empty_docs <- which(rq2_row_sums == 0)

# Check how many empty documents were found
length(empty_docs)
```


```{r}
#Step 3.1: Remove empty documents

# Identify documents that still contain at least one term
non_empty_docs <- rq2_row_sums > 0

# Remove empty documents from the TF-IDF matrix
rq2_matrix <- rq2_matrix[
  non_empty_docs,
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

# Remove the same documents from the Q2 metadata
# to keep posts aligned with their link-sharing status
rq2_data <- rq2_data[
  non_empty_docs,
]

# Check the remaining dimensions
dim(rq2_matrix)
dim(rq2_data)

# Confirm that each document still matches one metadata row
nrow(rq2_matrix) == nrow(rq2_data)
```


```{r}
# Step 4 - Create a reproducible sample for clustering

# Fix the random seed so the same sample is selected every time
set.seed(123)

# Select 1,000 posts from the 6,418 non-empty documents
sample_size <- 1000

sample_id <- sample(
  1:nrow(rq2_matrix),
  sample_size,
  replace = FALSE
)

# Create the sampled TF-IDF matrix
rq2_sample_matrix <- rq2_matrix[
  sample_id,
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

# Keep the matching metadata rows
rq2_sample_data <- rq2_data[
  sample_id,
]

# Check dimensions
dim(rq2_sample_matrix)
dim(rq2_sample_data)

# Confirm that text vectors and metadata remain aligned
nrow(rq2_sample_matrix) == nrow(rq2_sample_data)
```

```{r}
# Compare link-sharing proportions in the full clustering data
# and the random sample
prop.table(table(rq2_data$has_link))

prop.table(table(rq2_sample_data$has_link))
```


```{r}
# Step 5 - Calculate cosine distance

# Normalise each TF-IDF document vector to unit length
rq2_norm_matrix <- diag(
  1 / sqrt(rowSums(rq2_sample_matrix^2))
) %*% rq2_sample_matrix

# Calculate cosine distance
rq2_distance <- dist(
  rq2_norm_matrix,
  method = "euclidean"
)^2 / 2

# Check the number of sampled documents
N <- nrow(rq2_sample_matrix)
N

# Check the dimensions of the distance matrix
dim(as.matrix(rq2_distance))
```

```{r}
# Step 6 - Project cosine distances into Euclidean space using MDS

# Number of sampled documents
N <- nrow(rq2_sample_matrix)

# Use a high-dimensional MDS representation for clustering
# to preserve as much of the cosine-distance information as possible
rq2_mds <- cmdscale(
  rq2_distance,
  k = N - 1
)

# Check the dimensions of the MDS representation
dim(rq2_mds)
```


```{r}
# Step 7 - Select the number of clusters using the Elbow Method

set.seed(123)

# Store the within-cluster sum of squares for 1 to 15 clusters
n <- 15
SSW <- rep(0, n)

for (a in 1:n) {
  
  K <- kmeans(
    rq2_mds,
    centers = a,
    nstart = 20
  )
  
  SSW[a] <- K$tot.withinss
}

# Display the SSW values
SSW

# Plot the elbow curve
plot(
  1:15,
  SSW,
  type = "b",
  xlab = "Number of Clusters",
  ylab = "Within-Cluster Sum of Squares (SSW)",
  main = "Elbow Method Using Cosine Distance and MDS"
)
```


```{r}
# Step 8 - Compare candidate cluster solutions

set.seed(123)

K3 <- kmeans(
  rq2_mds,
  centers = 3,
  nstart = 20
)

K4 <- kmeans(
  rq2_mds,
  centers = 4,
  nstart = 20
)

K5 <- kmeans(
  rq2_mds,
  centers = 5,
  nstart = 20
)

# Compare cluster sizes
table(K3$cluster)
table(K4$cluster)
table(K5$cluster)
```


```{r}
# Step 9 - Inspect top terms for candidate cluster solutions

show_top_terms <- function(K, matrix, top_n = 10) {
  
  for (cluster_number in sort(unique(K$cluster))) {
    
    # Identify posts assigned to the current cluster
    cluster_posts_id <- which(
      K$cluster == cluster_number
    )
    
    # Extract their original TF-IDF document vectors
    cluster_posts <- matrix[
      cluster_posts_id,
      ,
      drop = FALSE
    ]
    
    # Calculate the mean TF-IDF weight of each term
    cluster_term_weight <- colMeans(
      cluster_posts
    )
    
    # Display the highest-weighted terms
    cat(
      "\nCluster",
      cluster_number,
      "-",
      length(cluster_posts_id),
      "posts\n"
    )
    
    print(
      sort(
        cluster_term_weight,
        decreasing = TRUE
      )[1:top_n]
    )
  }
}
```


```{r}
# Top terms for k = 3
show_top_terms(
  K3,
  rq2_sample_matrix
)
```

```{r}
# Top terms for k = 4
show_top_terms(
  K4,
  rq2_sample_matrix
)
```

```{r}
# Top terms for k = 5
show_top_terms(
  K5,
  rq2_sample_matrix
)
```

```{r}
# Step 10 - Inspect representative posts for the selected k = 4 solution

# Store the selected clustering solution
K <- K4

# Add cluster assignments to the sampled metadata
rq2_sample_data$cluster <- K$cluster

# Inspect a small number of original posts from each cluster
for (cluster_number in 1:4) {
  
  cat("\n\n--- Cluster", cluster_number, "---\n")
  
  cluster_posts <- rq2_sample_data[
    rq2_sample_data$cluster == cluster_number,
  ]
  
  print(
    head(
      cluster_posts$text,
      10
    )
  )
}
```


```{r}
# Step 11 - Visualise the selected four-cluster solution

# Use the selected k = 4 solution
K <- K4

# Create a two-dimensional MDS representation for visualisation only
rq2_mds2 <- cmdscale(
  rq2_distance,
  k = 2
)

# Plot posts using their final cluster assignments
plot(
  rq2_mds2,
  col = K$cluster,
  pch = 16,
  xlab = "MDS Dimension 1",
  ylab = "MDS Dimension 2",
  main = "Four Thematic Clusters in Cyclone Alfred Discussion"
)

# Add cluster labels
legend(
  "bottomright",
  legend = c(
    "1 General discussion",
    "2 Safety and preparedness",
    "3 Impacts and outages",
    "4 Tracking and updates"
  ),
  col = 1:4,
  pch = 16,
  cex = 0.7
)
```


```{r}
# Step 12 - Examine link-sharing across thematic clusters

# Assign the final cluster labels to the sampled posts
rq2_sample_data$cluster <- factor(K$cluster)

# Create a contingency table of cluster and link-sharing status
link_table <- table(
  rq2_sample_data$cluster,
  rq2_sample_data$has_link
)

# Display the number of posts with and without links
link_table

# Calculate link-sharing proportions within each cluster
link_proportions <- prop.table(
  link_table,
  margin = 1
)

# Display percentages for easier comparison
round(link_proportions * 100, 2)
```

```{r}
# Step 13 - Test the association between cluster and link sharing

# Perform a chi-squared test of independence
link_chisq <- chisq.test(link_table)

# Display the test result
link_chisq

# Check expected frequencies
link_chisq$expected

# Extract the p-value
link_chisq$p.value
```
